items.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: So eventually I went with Red Norvo. We rehearsed for three months... So Red Norvo and Mildred Bailey came in one night and he said, “I’m starting a band do you want to come with us?” So I said sure.

ctx.x: Well mostly buses, yeah, or cars, a lot by car. So eventually I went with Red Norvo. We rehearsed for three months in a place called Odd Fellows Hall, and it was on 48th Street. We rehearsed for three months in that. Guys from Duke’s band would come by. Because Red was well known at that time. But this was like, he had a band from Pittsburgh and he had heard me jamming in a place which was across the street from where Sweet Basil’s is now. And we used to go in there and jam, it was with a guy, I don’t know if you…
Wow. That was your first recorded solo, wasn’t it? With him?

items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: met Eddie Bert down at the Village and we'd become friends. And so I formed a little band

ctx.x: Then, it was during this period that -- that I started a small band. And I'd be -- met Eddie Bert down at the Village and we'd become friends. And so I formed a little band and we went to a job on 52nd Street. AT the Downbeat Club, I think it was. And we went in with Billie Holiday. I had Shorty Rogers, Eddie Bert, Aaron Sax, Hank Kahout, Specs Powell, Clyde Lombardi.
